newsitem.title: USA: N.J. ruling on pensions could cost $50 mln - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. ruling on pensions could cost $50 mln - paper.

text.p: A New Jersey appeals court panel is set to hear arguments in a pension case that could cost local governments $50 million in extra benefits, the Star Ledger reported Tuesday.

At issue is whether attorneys who work for the state can switch from the Public Employees Retirement System to the Police and Firemen's Retirement System, which provides a more costly retirement package.

If the court rules against the state, it could cost New Jersey local governments about $50 million, the paper said. Union County alone would have to pay $4.35 million retroactively and about $405,000 annually to meet the increased requirement.
Briefs in the case are due before the Appellate Division of the state Superior Court the first week of December.
